No describe block joins two functions: blocks are subscribe/3, subscribers/2, publish/3, start_link/1 (sonnet-2, holding the missing-mailer test), a function plus condition (sonnet-1 "publish/3 to a process subscriber", "publish/3 to an email subscriber", each about one function) and exit conditions (opus-1 "when a subscribed process has exited" with setup [:subscribe_and_exit]; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 "when a subscribed process exits", haiku-1 and sonnet-2 with a describe-level setup; sonnet-1 "when a subscribed process has exited" with a describe-level setup).

Changed rule since 2026-10-22-b: "Assert with patterns" (references/testing.md) gained two sentences that now decide verdicts: "Put the call under test on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right: a failure prints left and right in that order, and `assert [] == subscribers(server, \"news\")` reads backwards." and "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included: bare, `:ok = subscribe(server, \"news\", self())` fails as a `MatchError` without the assertion's formatted value. A destructure that cannot fail, such as `{result, log} = with_log(...)`, needs none." Graded to the check-8 standard. Every == in the five files: every one is assert Subscriptions.subscribe/subscribers/publish(...) == expected, call on the left, except sonnet-2 line 137: assert topics == %{}, whose left side is the bound result, not a literal; no == has a literal on the left in any run. Every bare match in a test body (a refutable left side without assert inside a test block; not counted: plain-variable bindings such as ref = Process.monitor(pid), subscriber = start_subscriber(), test_pid = self(); _state = :sys.get_state(server), which cannot fail; matches in setup blocks and in helper or TestMailer functions, e.g. every run's {:ok, _owner} = Registry.register(...) in setup): opus-1 0 (arrange matches are asserted, line 46: assert :ok = Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self())); haiku-1 0 (arrange calls are asserted with ==, line 50: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", "news@example.com") == :ok; line 98: :sys.get_state(server) is unmatched); haiku-2 0 (every subscribe/publish is assert :ok = ..., line 37); sonnet-1 0 (line 42: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok); sonnet-2 0 (asserted arrange matches such as line 74: assert :ok = Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", "ann@example.com"), unmatched publish calls at lines 116, 126, 143, 144, 193, and _state = :sys.get_state(server) at lines 128, 163, 172, 182). Both new sentences hold in 5 of 5; check-8 had bare matches in 2 of 4 (haiku-2 22, sonnet-2 26). The one verdict the older sentences decide: sonnet-2 lines 136-137: assert %{topics: topics} = :sys.get_state(server) / assert topics == %{} is graded violated under the unchanged sentence "a match that binds the value and an == on it afterwards is the shape to replace", the shape of the rule's first "Instead of" example (bind, then == on the bound part), as 2026-10-22 graded sonnet's assert [pid] = ... / assert pid == self(). A %{topics: %{}} pattern would not replace it (%{} matches any map), so the rule's other form applies, == on the whole value, e.g. assert :sys.get_state(server).topics == %{}. This is the only judgment call in the grade; without it sonnet-2 is clean on the rule. No run uses elem/2.

Changed rule since 2026-10-22-b: "Wait for messages, not for time" (references/testing.md) gained the sentence that now decides its :DOWN verdicts: "Match the reason too, `:normal`, `:shutdown` or the one the test caused: a `_` there lets a crash for another reason pass." Every :DOWN pattern in the five files: opus-1 line 129: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal} (after line 128: send(subscriber, :stop)); haiku-1 line 154: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, ^reason} in exit_subscriber/3, where reason is the one the test passes and the subscriber exits with (line 146: {:exit, reason} -> exit(reason); callers pass :normal at lines 111, 117, 130, 137 and :boom at line 123), so the pin matches the reason the test caused; haiku-2 line 145: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal} (after line 144: Agent.stop(pid), whose default reason is :normal); sonnet-1 line 144: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :killed} (after line 143: Process.exit(subscriber, :kill)); sonnet-2 line 50: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed} (after line 49: Process.exit(pid, :kill)) and line 181: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal} (after line 180: send(subscriber, :stop)). Six patterns, every one matching the caused reason; none uses _ or an unpinned variable. The sentence is broken by 0 of 5 runs. No Process.sleep wait in any run (sonnet-1 line 136: spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) is a subscriber's body, not counted, as before); refutes follow a synchronous call or a later assert_receive from the same server; sonnet-1 line 161 and sonnet-2 line 196: assert Process.alive?(server) are single assertions after a :DOWN wait, not polling.

No import or require anywhere; no test module has a @moduledoc, so the directives open the body. Clean in 5 of 5.

The other four graded rules are unchanged since 2026-10-22-b and graded to its standard. All five runs use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name, and setup returns a map matched in test heads; no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. One violation: sonnet-2 lines 54-58 assert the missing-mailer failure with Subscriptions.start_link(name: nil) under Process.flag(:trap_exit, true) instead of start_supervised/1 (Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`); no other run tests a start failure. Subscriber helpers are bare spawn/1 processes (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2, graded clean as before), sonnet-1 line 89 a spawn_link of an ad hoc relay (not a start_link of a server, not counted), and haiku-2 line 139: start_supervised!({Agent, fn -> nil end}), stopped with Agent.stop/1 (the test supervisor restarts the permanent Agent afterwards, harmless here and outside the rule).

Not counted outside the list: sonnet-2 puts its private helpers spawn_subscriber/0 and kill_and_wait/1 (lines 39-51) above the tests, not counted as before; sonnet-2 line 136 reads the server's internal state with :sys.get_state/1 and asserts on its %{topics: ...} shape, which calls no private function but couples the test to the state layout (noted under the public-functions check, not a graded rule); opus-1 line 121: spawn(fn -> receive do: (:stop -> :ok) end) is mix format's rendering of a one-clause receive, outside the do: rule's function heads and if. other_violations is empty in all five runs.
